title: Soft Landing
pin_title: ADHD Soft Landing After Work: One Calm Ritual So Your Evening Starts Gently
description: Walking in the door with a full brain can make the rest of the day feel heavy. Choose one gentle ritual to land: hang your bag, drink a glass of water, or sit for two minutes. Do only that before anything else. A tiny ritual tells your body the work day is finished and the evening can begin without pressure. Keep it so small that skipping it feels silly. #ADHD #EveningRoutine #SelfCare #ADHDTips

title: One Drawer Only
pin_title: ADHD One Drawer Rule: Empty Just One Drawer Today So Clutter Feels Possible
description: A whole room of clutter can freeze you. Pick one single drawer and empty it onto the floor. Sort into keep, trash, and later in ten minutes. Put the keep items back. One finished drawer is a real win you can see. Tomorrow you can choose another if you want. Progress is still progress when the rest of the room waits. #ADHD #Organization #Clutter #ADHDTips

title: Kind Note to Self
pin_title: ADHD Kind Note to Self: Leave a Gentle Reminder Where You Will See It Tomorrow
description: Hard days make self-talk sharp. Write one kind sentence on a sticky note and place it where tomorrow-you will find it, like the fridge or the desk. Something simple like you did enough today. Reading it later is a soft restart. The note is a gift from past-you to future-you, so keep the words short and true. #ADHD #SelfCompassion #ADHDTips #Kindness

title: Phone Away
pin_title: ADHD Phone in Another Room: Leave It So Focus Has a Chance
description: The phone on the desk keeps pulling attention. Put it in another room or a drawer while you do one short task. The distance makes checking harder than just continuing. When the task ends you can go get it. Many people find the first ten minutes feel different without the device nearby. #ADHD #Focus #ADHDTips #Distraction

title: One Page Only
pin_title: ADHD One Page Only: Write or Read Just One Page and Stop
description: A whole chapter or list can feel heavy. Promise yourself only one page. Open the book or notebook, finish that single page, and close it. The small finish is still a finish, and a page is an end you can actually see. Often the next page feels easier after the first one is done, but you are allowed to stop. #ADHD #Reading #ADHDTips #Starting
